newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.S. vetoes draft on Israel building in E.Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: U.S. vetoes draft on Israel building in E.Jerusalem.

text.p: The United States on Friday vetoed a Security Council resolution drafted by its European Union allies calling on Israel to abandon plans to build a new Jewish neighborhood in mostly Arab East Jerusalem.
The vote was 14 in favor, with only the United States voting against.
As one of the council's five permanent members, the negative U.S. vote killed the resolution, drafted by Britain, France, Portugal and Sweden.

The veto followed a council debate on Wednesday and Thursday in which virtually all the nearly 50 speakers condemned Israel's plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews on a tree-covered hill between East Jerusalem and Bethlehem that Israel captured during the 1967 Middle East war. The site is called Har Homa by Israel and Jabal Abu Ghneim by the Palestinians.
The United States also criticised Israel's action but said it opposed any council action that might hinder the Middle East negotiations.
Israel regards the entire city of Jerusalem as its undivided capital while the Palestinians see East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
